title: Locally Deployed Large Language Models for AI-Assisted Outpatient Prescription Review: Crossover Study.
comparator: Unaided pharmacist review and stand-alone AI review
results: Absolute reduction in hallucination rate=15.0 percentage points; Accuracy=97.2% (human-AI collaborative) vs 82.6% (pharmacist-alone); Sensitivity=98% (human-AI collaborative) vs 55% (pharmacist-alone)
main_finding: Knowledge-augmented LLM significantly reduced hallucination rates and improved factual accuracy and sensitivity in pharmacist-led outpatient prescription review.

title: Private LLM and RAG Chatbot
method: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system combining a publicly deployed LLM with semantic document retrieval
results: Reduction in hallucinations=Reported as part of a controlled comparison against three baseline systems, with direct measurement of the reduction in hallucinations on a curated set of 300 queries from an enterprise corpus consisting of 500 documents; Accuracy=93.5%
main_finding: The hybrid RAG system significantly reduces hallucinations and improves factual accuracy, achieving an accuracy of 93.5% in business knowledge retrieval.

title: AGRAG: Advanced Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation for LLMs
design: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework with graph-based reasoning.
data: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 LLM on 2080Ti GPU, with low resource setting (-L) and four datasets (Novel, Medical, WOS, IFS-Rel).
method: AGRAG: Advanced Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation with MCMI subgraph generation and statistics-based entity extraction.
results: Hallucinated prediction rate=AGRAG achieves the lowest rate by leveraging MCMI subgraphs to provide explicit evidence for retrieved chunks.; ACC (Accuracy)=AGRAG-L achieves higher ACC than SiReRAG-L and HippoRAG2-L across multiple tasks.; ROG (ROUGE-L)=AGRAG-L achieves higher ROG than SiReRAG-L and HippoRAG2-L across multiple tasks.
main_finding: AGRAG reduces hallucinations and improves factual accuracy, coherence, and relevance of generated text compared to SiReRAG-L and HippoRAG2-L.

title: Advancing Arabic Medical Question Answering Systems with RAG and LLMs Integration
design: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) integration with Large Language Models (LLMs) in Arabic medical question-answering (QA) systems.
method: Integration of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with Large Language Models (LLMs) for Arabic medical QA systems.
comparator: Base model performance, fine-tuned version of the model.
results: Accuracy=95.6% (base model) to 97.8% (fine-tuned) to 98.7% (RAG-enhanced); F-measure=90.4% (base model) to 93.7% (fine-tuned) to 97.6% (RAG-enhanced)
main_finding: RAG integration with LLMs significantly improves accuracy and F-measure in Arabic medical QA systems, suggesting a reduction in hallucinations and enhanced factual consistency.
